<?php

function getLastChildGoingHome(array $inputs, int $candies): int {
    for ($i = 0; $i < count($inputs); $i++) {
        if ($inputs[$i] % $candies == 0) {
            $inputs[$i] = $inputs[$i] / $candies;
        } else {
            $inputs[$i] = (int)($inputs[$i] / $candies) + 1;
        }
    }

    $last = 0;
    $lastIdx = 0;

    for ($i = 0; $i < count($inputs); $i++) {
        if ($inputs[$i] >= $last) {
            $last = $inputs[$i];
            $lastIdx = $i;
        }
    }

    return $lastIdx + 1;
}

function main() {
    $line = fgets(STDIN);
    if ($line === false) return;
    $parts = explode(' ', trim($line));
    $n1 = (int)$parts[0];
    $n2 = (int)$parts[1];

    $line = fgets(STDIN);
    if ($line === false) return;
    $n = (int)trim($line);

    $idx = ($n - 1) % 6;
    $neg = false;
    $current = $n1;

    if ($idx >= 3) {
        $neg = true;
        $idx = $idx - 3;
    }

    if ($idx == 1) {
        $current = $n2;
    } else if ($idx == 2) {
        $current = $n2 - $n1;
    }

    if ($neg) {
        $current = $current * -1;
    }

    $mod = 1000000007;
    $result = ($current % $mod + $mod) % $mod;
    echo $result . "\n";
}

main();

class Input {
    private static $line;

    public static function next() {
        self::$line = fgets(STDIN);
        return self::$line !== false && self::$line !== '';
    }

    public static function nextLong(&$a) {
        $ok = self::next();
        $a = $ok ? (int)trim(self::$line) : 0;
        return $ok;
    }

    public static function nextTwoLongs(&$a, &$b) {
        $ok = self::next();
        if ($ok) {
            $parts = explode(' ', trim(self::$line));
            $a = (int)$parts[0];
            $b = (int)$parts[1];
        } else {
            $a = 0;
            $b = 0;
        }
        return $ok;
    }

source_data.prob_desc_description: Jzzhu has invented a kind of sequences, they meet the following property:You are given x and y, please calculate fn modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Output a single integer representing fn modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line contains two integers x and y (|x|, |y| ≤ 109). The second line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·109).
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first sample, f2 = f1 + f3, 3 = 2 + f3, f3 = 1.In the second sample, f2 =  - 1;  - 1 modulo (109 + 7) equals (109 + 6).
